dedupe_keys.name: icao aircraft engine emissions databank hosted by easa

description: The ICAO Aircraft Engine Emissions Databank holds the exhaust emissions of production aircraft engines, measured and certified under ICAO Annex 16 Volume II. It covers turbojet and turbofan engines with rated static thrust above 26.7 kN, giving gaseous emissions, smoke and non-volatile particulate matter per engine. EASA hosts the databank on behalf of ICAO. The data come from the engine manufacturers, who submit them after approval by the primary certificating authority using an Excel template; EASA checks format and consistency, and the manufacturers remain solely responsible for accuracy. The page states the databank is updated at least once a year. Downloads on 2026-09-28: the Emissions Databank spreadsheet and record of changes (March 2026), a zip of engine datasheets (June 2025), submission templates for gaseous and smoke data and for nvPM (June 2025) and an introduction (June 2023). Coverage: engines in production worldwide. Format and access: Excel and PDF downloads without registration. Licence and cost: free; no reuse licence is stated. Caveats: values are certification test results at standard thrust settings, not in-service measurements, and smaller engines are outside scope. It supports emissions inventories and climate scenarios for airport and air network studies. It relates to the EUROCONTROL BADA and OpenAP performance models and to the FAA AEDT platform in the catalogue, which use engine emissions indices.
